from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisites & Definitions", [
            "Planar graphs avoid edge crossings.",
            "Vertices, edges, and faces are fundamental components.",
            "Visualize a simple triangular planar graph."
        ])
        
        # Setup the graph elements
        v1 = Dot(color=WHITE)
        v2 = Dot(color=WHITE)
        v3 = Dot(color=WHITE)
        
        # Positions
        v1.move_to(self.grid["B3"])
        v2.move_to(self.grid["D2"])
        v3.move_to(self.grid["D4"])
        
        e1 = Line(v1.get_center(), v2.get_center(), color="#00FFFF")
        e2 = Line(v2.get_center(), v3.get_center(), color="#00FFFF")
        e3 = Line(v3.get_center(), v1.get_center(), color="#00FFFF")
        
        face_inner = Polygon(v1.get_center(), v2.get_center(), v3.get_center(), color="#FF00FF", fill_opacity=0.3)
        
        v_label = Text("V", font_size=20, color=WHITE).next_to(v1, UP, buff=0.1)
        e_label = Text("E", font_size=20, color="#00FFFF").next_to(e1, LEFT, buff=0.1)
        f_label = Text("F", font_size=20, color="#FF00FF").move_to(face_inner.get_center())

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(Create(v1), Create(v2), Create(v3), Write(v_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(Create(e1), Create(e2), Create(e3), Write(e_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(FadeIn(face_inner), Write(f_label))
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Euler’s Characteristic Formula", [
            "Euler's formula states V minus E plus F equals 2.",
            "This constant invariant holds for connected planar graphs.",
            "A square with a diagonal validates the formula."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        formula = MathTex(r"V - E + F = 2", color="#FFFF00")
        self.place_at_grid(formula, "B3", scale_factor=1.5)
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Square graph construction
        nodes = [Dot(self.grid[pos]) for pos in ["D3", "D5", "F3", "F5"]]
        edges = [
            Line(nodes[0].get_center(), nodes[1].get_center(), color="#00FF00"),
            Line(nodes[1].get_center(), nodes[3].get_center(), color="#00FF00"),
            Line(nodes[3].get_center(), nodes[2].get_center(), color="#00FF00"),
            Line(nodes[2].get_center(), nodes[0].get_center(), color="#00FF00"),
            Line(nodes[0].get_center(), nodes[3].get_center(), color="#00FF00")
        ]
        graph = VGroup(*nodes, *edges)
        self.play(Create(graph))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        stats = MathTex(r"V=4, E=5, F=3", color="#FF0000")
        calc = MathTex(r"4 - 5 + 3 = 2", color="#FFFFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(stats, "A3", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(calc, "E3", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(stats))
        self.play(Indicate(stats))
        self.play(Write(calc))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF0000"))
        
        final_result = calc[-1]
        self.play(final_result.animate.scale(2.0).set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Concept of Dual Graphs", [
            "Dual graphs transform faces into new vertices.",
            "Connect vertices if their faces share an edge.",
            "Hexagonal honeybee grids form triangular dual lattices."
        ])
        
        # Original graph setup
        # Represent a simple planar graph: a square with a diagonal (2 faces)
        nodes = VGroup(*[Dot(color=WHITE) for _ in range(4)])
        self.place_at_grid(nodes[0], 'C2')
        self.place_at_grid(nodes[1], 'C4')
        self.place_at_grid(nodes[2], 'E4')
        self.place_at_grid(nodes[3], 'E2')
        
        edges = VGroup(
            Line(nodes[0].get_center(), nodes[1].get_center(), color="#00FFFF"),
            Line(nodes[1].get_center(), nodes[2].get_center(), color="#00FFFF"),
            Line(nodes[2].get_center(), nodes[3].get_center(), color="#00FFFF"),
            Line(nodes[3].get_center(), nodes[0].get_center(), color="#00FFFF"),
            Line(nodes[0].get_center(), nodes[2].get_center(), color="#00FFFF")
        )
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(nodes), Create(edges))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FF0000")
        
        # Dual vertices
        dual_nodes = VGroup(
            Dot(color="#FF0000").move_to(np.array([4.3, 0.6, 0])), # face 1
            Dot(color="#FF0000").move_to(np.array([5.1, 1.4, 0]))  # face 2
        )
        
        self.play(FadeIn(dual_nodes))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFF00")
        
        dual_edge = DashedLine(dual_nodes[0].get_center(), dual_nodes[1].get_center(), color="#FFFF00")
        self.play(Create(dual_edge))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FF00")
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [

        ]
        self.setup_layout("Duality Mechanics & Symmetry", lecture_lines)
        
        # Setup visual elements
        square = Square(color=BLUE)

        eq_text = MathTex(r"V_{dual} = F_{original}", color="#00FF00")
        self.place_at_grid(eq_text, 'E3', scale_factor=0.6)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Application & Wrap-up", [
            "Duality helps solve complex routing problems.",
            "Shifting from nodes to regions optimizes paths.",
            "Use dual graphs for efficient network design."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show a maze-like warehouse layout grid
        grid_lines = VGroup()
        for i in range(5):
            h_line = Line(start=self.grid["B1"], end=self.grid["B6"])
            h_line.shift(DOWN * i * 0.8)
            grid_lines.add(h_line)
            v_line = Line(start=self.grid["B1"], end=self.grid["F1"])
            v_line.shift(RIGHT * i * 1)
            grid_lines.add(v_line)
            
        grid_lines.set_color("#00FFFF")
        self.play(Create(grid_lines))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#00FFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Animate a robot path using the dual graph
        robot = Dot(color="#FFFF00")
        robot.move_to(self.grid["C2"])
        path = VMobject(color="#FFFF00").set_points_as_corners([
            self.grid["C2"], self.grid["C4"], self.grid["E4"], self.grid["E2"]
        ])
        self.play(Create(robot), Create(path))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFF00")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Overlay final application summary text
        summary = Text("Dual Graph Network", font_size=24, color="#FFFFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(summary, "A3")
        self.play(FadeIn(summary))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Unlocking Planar Graphs: Euler's Formula and Duality

sections.title: Prerequisites & Definitions
sections.content: Define a planar graph (can be drawn in a 2D plane without edges crossing) and identify the three fundamental components: Vertices (V), Edges (E), and Faces (F).
sections.example: Visualize a simple triangle graph: 3 vertices, 3 edges, and 2 faces (the inner triangle and the infinite exterior region).

sections.title: Euler’s Characteristic Formula
sections.content: Introduce the formula V - E + F = 2. Explain how this invariant constant holds for any connected planar graph regardless of its complexity.
sections.example: Demonstrate with a square with one diagonal (4 vertices, 5 edges, 3 faces): 4 - 5 + 3 = 2. It holds perfectly!

sections.title: The Concept of Dual Graphs
sections.content: Explain the geometric transformation: place a node in each face of the original graph and connect nodes if their respective faces share an edge.
sections.example: Imagine a honeybee hive (hexagonal grid). The dual graph turns every hexagonal cell into a vertex, creating a triangular lattice connecting the centers.

sections.title: Duality Mechanics & Symmetry
sections.content: Show the transformation rules: V_dual = F_original, F_dual = V_original, and E_dual = E_original. Explain that duality is a reciprocal relationship.
sections.example: Transform a 3D-projected cube (8 vertices, 12 edges, 6 faces) into its dual: the Octahedron (6 vertices, 12 edges, 8 faces).

sections.title: Application & Wrap-up
sections.content: Connect duality to real-world circuit layout or network design, where shifting from nodes to regions helps solve complex routing problems.
sections.example: Using dual graphs to optimize the pathing of a delivery robot navigating through distinct zones (faces) of a warehouse floor.
